decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom took substantial development investment, was publicly launched with a staged US release, and supports the firm's high-end QA direction, so management attributes any slow uptake to the long sales cycles of proton centers and stays committed.
Having already withdrawn one small volume chamber, management sees the remaining small volume chamber as the justified choice in that segment and keeps it as a core precision dosimetry product.
The multi-model standard clinical chamber line is central to the firm's established calibration and dosimetry business and has strong ongoing demand, so it stays.
The relative dosimetry chamber is tied into the firm's water phantom and connected QA workflows, so dropping it would undercut the announced integrated platform direction.
Thimble chambers are staple reference instruments backed by accredited calibration services with steady demand and low upkeep, so the firm keeps it.
